questions.q: Which question does data governance answer, per the lesson?
options: Who decides, and what's the rule?
Is this specific dataset correct right now?
How do we physically store this data?
Which cloud vendor should we use?
questions.explain: Governance is the rulebook — who decides and what the policy is. Management is the day-to-day doing; quality is the measurable scorecard.

questions.q: Where does DAMA-DMBOK place data governance relative to its other knowledge areas?
options: At the center of the wheel, with the other knowledge areas arranged around it
As a minor footnote with no real role
Outside the wheel entirely, as an unrelated discipline
Tied for last place in priority with data security
questions.explain: DAMA-DMBOK's wheel diagram puts governance at the hub, deliberately framing it as what gives the other ten knowledge areas their authority.

questions.q: What failure pattern does the lesson describe when a company buys a data catalog and calls it 'governance'?
options: Conflicting metric definitions persist because the tool never answered who decides
The company immediately achieves perfect data quality
All data management work becomes unnecessary
Regulatory compliance is automatically satisfied
questions.explain: A tool doesn't resolve a governance question by itself — buying software isn't the same as establishing decision rights and accountability.

questions.q: Per DAMA's own definition cited in the lesson, what is data quality management?
options: Planning, implementation, and control of activities that apply quality management techniques to data
The exclusive responsibility of the governance council
A synonym for data governance itself
A one-time audit performed before a system launch
questions.explain: DAMA defines data quality management as a specific operational discipline — distinct from governance, which sets the rules it operates under.

questions.q: A manager asks 'should IT be blamed for this bad report?' and investigation shows no one ever defined what a correct value should look like. Using the lesson's quick test, what kind of problem is this?
options: A governance gap, not an execution gap
A hardware failure
A data management success
An unsolvable problem with no root cause
questions.explain: The quick test asks whether this is a rules disagreement, a handling breakdown, or a factual defect — no defined 'correct' value is a governance gap.
